annotationRationale: Both methods combine right-triangle lengths with pyramid volume. The integer restriction is resolved either by complete factor-pair enumeration or by a distinct bound using the gap between odd squares.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate. The integer restriction is an essential supporting number-theoretic feature, not a reason to change the area.

review.questionCheck: Independent Pythagorean elimination gives slant lengths 7, 9, 11 and height 3. The base side squares are 40 and 72, giving volume 24√5, choice A. The stem and key agree, and the spatial relationships are adequately specified without a figure.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: There are no shared-bank methods. Both useful supplied routes are retained: complete difference-of-squares factor enumeration and a distinct bound using odd-square spacing. LIVE and AoPS Solution 2 support the common geometric equation. No further accessible route is needed.
review.annotationCheck: Integer-equation completeness and pyramid volume are appropriate assessed concepts, with Pythagorean lengths and rectangle area as support. The method-specific factorization and square-comparison nodes distinguish the two integer arguments.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate. The integer restriction is an essential supporting number-theoretic feature, not a reason to change the area.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Pythagorean elimination correctly gives h² = (k−2)²−16. Positivity forces k ≥ 7 and makes both factors positive. Of (1,16), (2,8), and (4,4), parity excludes the first and positive height excludes the last. The remaining pair gives k = 7 and h = 3, followed by the correct base area and volume 24√5.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The method accurately follows the mathematical route in LIVE and AoPS Solution 2, with original explanatory prose and explicit completeness checks. It does not inherit AoPS Solution 1's erroneous displayed assignment of its variables. The third-party basis is correctly labeled source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The perpendicularity explains the first move, all right-triangle equations are stated, and positivity, parity, and the zero-height exclusion are justified. The volume formula is explained at use.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_174, math:integer-diophantine-equations, cnm_152, cnm_p089, and cnm_h111 all correspond directly to written steps.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native Pythagorean, difference-of-squares, rectangle-area, and simple-solid-volume links apply. The integer-equation synthesis has no supplied CN link.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 8.G.B.7 supports the spatial right-triangle work, A-SSE.A.2 the factorization, and G-GMD.A.3 the pyramid-volume application. The elementary area links support the formula only; their tiling requirements and G-GMD.A.1's volume derivations are not demonstrated.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: Every direct node is supported. The integer-solution node captures the complete factor-pair restriction rather than merely a real quadratic calculation.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The equation h² = t(t−8) gives t ≥ 9. Since t and h are odd and 0 < h < t−4, h ≤ t−6. Squaring positive quantities gives 4t ≤ 36, hence t = 9 and h = 3. The resulting side squares and volume are correct, and the bounds exclude every other admissible integer value.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The common height equation is correctly credited to LIVE and AoPS Solution 2. The odd-square bound is honestly described as a separately developed alternative, rather than attributed to those references as their argument.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The parity inference, minimum gap of two between distinct odd integers, and positivity needed before squaring are all explicit. This method independently reaches the volume.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: The geometric and integer-equation nodes match the proof. cnm_079 supports comparison through positive squares; the parity restriction and completeness belong to math:integer-diophantine-equations.
